fixes.explanation: Rain and rivers aren't what the text names here. The LORD thunders from heaven, and the voice of the Most High resounded with "hailstones and coals of fire." (Psalm 18:13). Hail and burning coals are what come down. I'd leave the umbrella home.

Wind and dust aren't named here. The text says the voice of the Most High resounded, and then it names "hailstones and coals of fire." (Psalm 18:13). David repeats the same two things in verse 12. So the answer is hailstones and coals of fire.

The heading does mention Saul, but David himself doesn't open by naming anybody. He starts with, "I love You, O LORD, my strength." (Psalm 18:1). I've seen bakers open a speech with a long list, and this one skips the list and goes straight to the love. That's a good order to put things in.

David says, "In my distress I called upon the LORD; I cried to my God for help." (Psalm 18:6). The cords of death have encompassed him and the torrents of chaos have overwhelmed him, and his move is to call. That's the whole plan. Sometimes the best plan is the shortest one.
Mount Sinai isn't in this verse. David says, "From His temple He heard my voice…" (Psalm 18:6). The LORD hears from His temple. So the answer is the temple.
The word isn't rested. David says, "He rescued me because He delighted in me." (Psalm 18:19). The LORD brought him out into the open because of delight.
Boasting isn't in this verse. David says, "He rescued me because He delighted in me." (Psalm 18:19). The word is delighted.
David says the opposite. "For I have kept the ways of the LORD and have not wickedly departed from my God." (Psalm 18:21). He kept them, and he says he didn't wickedly depart from his God.
The verse says the opposite. David says, "You broaden the path beneath me so that my ankles do not give way." (Psalm 18:36). The LORD makes the path wider, not narrower. Broadens is the word.
Joab isn't named in this song at all. David says, "You have armed me with strength for battle; You have subdued my foes beneath me." (Psalm 18:39). The "You" is the LORD. David gives Him the credit.
David says, "a people I had not known shall serve me." (Psalm 18:43). A people he had not known will serve him. I think that's quite a turn. The LORD has made him head of nations.
That's not what the verse says. David says, "a people I had not known shall serve me." (Psalm 18:43). Serving is the word. That's what this people will do.
David says, "When they hear me, they obey me; foreigners cower before me." (Psalm 18:44). Cower means shrinking back. The same verse says they hear him and they obey.
David says, "You exalt me above my foes; You rescue me from violent men." (Psalm 18:48). The LORD lifts him above his foes and rescues him from violent men. I think that's good news for David.
